# InternetSecureAreaProcess

**What it does.** Single run. Goes through the PDD sections “Acesso” → “Área segura”. No inputs.

**Secrets** (environment variables, never in the project): `NK_SECRET_CREDENCIAL_SENHA`, `NK_SECRET_CREDENCIAL_USUARIO`.

Names in the code are in English. Page labels, list columns, spreadsheet headers, secret names and rejection codes
stay as they are: they are data and contracts (the mapping is in `manifest.json` → `naming`).

## How it is organized

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `automation/pages.py` | one class per screen: `AccessPage`, `SecureAreaPage` |
| `automation/process.py` | `InternetSecureAreaProcess`: the order of the screens |
| `automation/selectors.py` | `SelectorKey` (one key per element) and how each element is located |
| `main.py` | command line |
| `selectors.json` | the same targets, read by the nekkora_rpa runtime (generated from the same plan; never edit by hand) |
| `manifest.json` | revisions, hashes, `step_id` ↔ Studio step map, names and keys |

## Screens and what each method does

- **`AccessPage`** — Screen of the PDD section “Acesso”.
  - `sign_in()` — Fills “Username” and “Password” with the credentials from the secret provider; clicks “Login”.
- **`SecureAreaPage`** — Screen of the PDD section “Área segura”: reads the text of the “Logout” link and clicks “Logout”.
  - `read_logout_link_text()` — Reads the text of the “Logout” link.
  - `click_logout()` — Clicks “Logout”.

## How each element is located

| Key | Strategy | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectorKey.ACCESS_USERNAME` | CSS `input#username` | id ou atributo de teste estável |
| `SelectorKey.ACCESS_PASSWORD` | CSS `input#password` | id ou atributo de teste estável |
| `SelectorKey.ACCESS_LOGIN` | XPATH `//form[@id="login"]//button[normalize-space(.)="Login"]` | XPath relacional |
| `SelectorKey.SECURE_AREA_LOGOUT` | XPATH `//a[normalize-space(.)="Logout"]` | XPath relacional |

nekkora_rpa acts only if the locator finds EXACTLY one element with the expected identity; none, or more than one, is an error (it never picks the first one).

## Run

The Nekkora Studio prepares the environment of this automation: **Desenvolver automação → Pendências → Preparar ambiente** (its own venv, `nekkora-rpa==0.2.0`, dependencies checked by hash, confirmation before installing).

```sh
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install "nekkora-rpa==0.2.0"
```
